builder_plan.scenario: You already need task-specific training and want to reduce its memory or compute cost.
builder_plan.change: Change only the training technique on a small controlled run after checking prerequisites.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current training recipe with the same model, data split, and evaluation.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Held-out quality, peak memory, training time, and full compute cost to the target quality.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: SOPO: Socratic Guided Policy Optimization for Span-Level Hallucination Detection
summary: SOPO replaces standard RLVR (e.g., GRPO) fine-tuning for span-level hallucination detection with a multi-turn RL loop in which a teacher model injects Socratic hints derived from ground truth during rollouts, plus turn-based advantage scaling to curb verbosity. The cost is a full RL training pipeline with a teacher model in the loop, rollout generation, and reward engineering, which is substantially more complex than supervised fine-tuning and difficult to run on a single 24 GB GPU. Adoption can fail through teacher-hint leakage that inflates training metrics without generalization, out-of-domain degradation, and dependence on ground-truth span annotations that most production settings lack.
rationale: The method requires multi-turn RL training with a teacher model and annotated hallucination spans, exceeding constrained infrastructure, so the reader should monitor it rather than adopt it now.
technique: Socratic teacher-guided RL for hallucination detection

claims.statement: SOPO replaces standard RLVR (e.g., GRPO) fine-tuning for span-level hallucination detection with a multi-turn RL loop in which a teacher model injects Socratic hints derived from ground truth during rollouts, plus turn-based advantage scaling to curb verbosity. The cost is a full RL training pipeline with a teacher model in the loop, rollout generation, and reward engineering, which is substantially more complex than supervised fine-tuning and difficult to run on a single 24 GB GPU. Adoption can fail through teacher-hint leakage that inflates training metrics without generalization, out-of-domain degradation, and dependence on ground-truth span annotations that most production settings lack.

SOPO (4B) reports state-of-the-art span-level hallucination detection on RAGTruth, surpassing GPT-5 and standard RL baselines, with higher mean scores than GRPO on four out-of-domain benchmarks and mixed evidence against CAPO; no multiplicative factor is stated.
